# svxreflector

**Conference server that links many SvxLink nodes into one talk group**

- **Version recorded:** 24.02
- **Categories:** `digital-modes`, `emcomm`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.svxlink.org>

## What it does

A server that SvxLink nodes connect to, relaying audio between all of them so that a transmission on any node is heard on the rest. It supports talk groups, so one server can carry several independent conversations, and it authenticates the nodes that connect.

## Why you would want it

Point-to-point links between repeaters do not scale past a handful. A reflector is the star-topology answer: every node connects to one place and the mesh problem disappears. If you are building a regional linked system rather than joining one, this is the piece in the middle.

## Before it will work

A machine reachable by the nodes, which in practice means a public address or a VPN, and the ports open. Node authentication keys, which you issue.

## How it installs

- apt: `svxreflector`

## Known problems

It is infrastructure other people depend on: an unreliable reflector takes a whole linked system down rather than one node. Audio quality is limited by the worst link in the group, not the average. As with svxlink-server the version spread across targets is wide and configuration syntax has changed between releases, so examples need checking against your version.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
